name: Core Data Layer Implementation
one_line_goal: Implement the approved schema as a tested, reactive, migration-safe local database that is already sync-ready.
objective: Build the local persistence layer - entities, repositories, seed data, validators, migrations and their tests - exactly as designed in SCHEMA.md, with no UI and no business logic.
rationale: Every later stage reads and writes through this layer. Defects here surface as irreproducible money bugs three stages later, so this stage is deliberately test-heavy and deliberately boring.
entry_criteria: SCHEMA.md approved and unchanged since Stage 2, or amended with an ADR.
The scaffold builds, the code generator runs, and the test harness passes.

how_to_work_this_stage.unit_of_work: One substage per working session. Work them strictly in listed order; do not parallelise or skip.
how_to_work_this_stage.between_substages: Tick the substage off, append evidence to docs/reports/STAGE_4_WORKLOG.md, then start the next. No user approval needed between substages.
how_to_work_this_stage.at_stage_end: The final substage assembles the stage report and stops for user approval before the next stage file is opened.
substage_list: 4.1 The Money type and core value types
4.2 Domain entities, enums and invalid-state prevention
4.3 Database schema definition and code generation
4.7 Seed data, suggested categories and the sink
4.10 Data layer test suite and performance smoke test
4.11 Data layer documentation and gate preparation

substages.name: The Money type and core value types
substages.goal: Implement a money value type that makes floating point arithmetic impossible by construction.
substages.why_it_matters: INV-01 is the invariant every other correctness property rests on. Enforcing it in a type is stronger than enforcing it in review.
entry_criteria: SCHEMA.md approved and unchanged since Stage 2, or amended with an ADR.
The scaffold builds, the code generator runs, and the test harness passes.

work.action: Implement Money as an immutable value type wrapping an int64 minor-unit amount plus a currency reference.
details: Provide no constructor, factory or setter that accepts a double or a num.
Provide a factory from a decimal string for parsing user input, which validates the decimal places against the currency exponent and returns a typed failure rather than truncating.

work.action: Implement arithmetic that cannot silently go wrong.
details: Addition, subtraction, negation, comparison.
Multiplication by an integer basis-point value with explicit floor and remainder outputs, because the allocation engine needs both.
Overflow detection on every operation, returning a typed failure at the documented maximum rather than wrapping.

work.action: Implement a Currency type holding the ISO 4217 code and minor unit exponent, with the exponent driving parsing and formatting.
details: Verify exponent 0, 2 and 3 behave correctly, since the seeded category names suggest a market where the exponent is not necessarily 2.

work.action: Implement BasisPoints as a value type constrained to 0 through 10000, rejecting out-of-range values at construction.
Implement a Clock interface and its real implementation, plus an IdGenerator interface and its UUID implementation.
details: Wire these to the fakes created in substage 3.8.

work.action: Write unit tests for every operation, including the boundary and failure cases.
details: Zero, one minor unit, the documented maximum, one beyond the maximum, negative values, mismatched currencies in an operation, and parsing input with too many decimal places.

acceptance_criteria: No public API on Money accepts or returns a double or num.
Every arithmetic operation has an overflow test that produces a typed failure rather than a wrapped value.
Parsing rejects more decimal places than the currency exponent allows, with a typed failure.
Operations across mismatched currencies are rejected.
Tests cover exponent 0, 2 and 3.
outputs: lib/domain/money/** with Money, Currency, BasisPoints, Clock, IdGenerator.
must_not: Do not add a convenience toDouble method - it will be used.
Do not allow arithmetic between different currencies.
common_pitfalls: A fromDouble factory added for test convenience, which then appears in production code.
Silent wrapping on overflow, which turns a large income into a negative balance.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Domain entities, enums and invalid-state prevention
substages.goal: Implement every entity as an immutable type that cannot be constructed in an invalid state.
substages.why_it_matters: The engine operates on these types; if an invalid entity can exist, the engine has to defend against it everywhere.
entry_criteria: Substage 4.1 (The Money type and core value types) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement immutable types for CategoryGroup, Category, Account, DistributionRuleVersion, RuleLine, IncomeEvent, Allocation, LedgerEntry, SpendingTransaction and AppSettings.
Implement CategoryType with the values resolved in OQ-03, and encode each type's headroom semantics as a method on the domain side.
details: The engine asks the category for its headroom rather than switching on a type code in three places.

work.action: Implement every other enumeration as a sealed type or enum with stable string serialisation, never ordinal.
Add validating factories that reject invalid states at construction.
details: Negative or zero ceiling when a ceiling is set.
Basis points outside 0 to 10000.
Empty or whitespace-only names.
A category whose redirect target is itself.
A FIXED_RECURRING category with no bill amount, or an anchor day outside 1 to 31.
A sink category that has a ceiling.

work.action: Implement equality, hashCode and copyWith on every entity so tests can compare by value.
Confirm the domain package compiles as pure Dart with no Flutter dependency, using the guard from substage 3.4.
Write unit tests proving each invalid construction is rejected with a typed failure rather than an exception.

acceptance_criteria: Every listed invalid construction is rejected, proven by a test.
No entity exposes a floating point monetary value.
Enumerations serialise as stable strings, proven by a round-trip test.
The layering guard passes on the domain package.
Headroom semantics live on the category type, not scattered across call sites.
must_not: Do not allow a public constructor that bypasses validation.
Do not store enums as ordinals.
common_pitfalls: Validation in a separate validator that callers can forget, rather than in the constructor.
copyWith that allows a valid entity to be copied into an invalid one.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Database schema definition and code generation
substages.goal: Transcribe SCHEMA.md into table definitions exactly, and prove the transcription is faithful.
substages.why_it_matters: Any divergence here invalidates the Stage 2 design review, silently.
entry_criteria: Substage 4.2 (Domain entities, enums and invalid-state prevention) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Define every table with the exact columns, types, nullability and defaults from the design.
details: Money as integer columns, percentages as integer basis points, timestamps as integer epoch milliseconds, ids as TEXT UUID.

work.action: Add the five sync columns to every synced table: updated_at_ms, updated_by_device, hlc, is_deleted, deleted_at_ms.
Enable foreign key enforcement explicitly at connection open, and prove it is on.
details: Many SQLite configurations leave it off by default, which silently permits orphan rows.
Write a test that attempts an orphan insert and expects it to fail.

work.action: Run the code generator and resolve every warning it produces rather than ignoring them.
Build the schema-versus-design comparison table.
details: One row per designed table and column, with the implemented type and a difference column.
This table goes into the stage report and is the evidence that the transcription is faithful.

work.action: Write an automated check that asserts no column in the database has a floating point storage class.
details: Read the schema at runtime rather than trusting the definition source, so a generator change cannot slip past.

work.action: Set the initial schema version constant and store it in app_settings.

acceptance_criteria: The comparison table shows no undocumented differences from SCHEMA.md.
A test proves foreign key enforcement is active by failing an orphan insert.
The automated floating-point check reads the live schema and passes.
Code generation completes with no unresolved warnings.
Every synced table carries all five sync columns.
outputs: lib/data/database/** with table definitions and generated code.
must_not: Do not silently deviate from SCHEMA.md - amend the document and note it.
Do not assume foreign keys are enforced.
common_pitfalls: A nullable column that the design marked required, which permits invalid rows the domain will later trip over.
Foreign keys defined but never enforced, so orphans accumulate until a report breaks.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Repository interfaces and CRUD implementation
substages.goal: Implement repository interfaces in the domain and their database-backed implementations in the data layer.
substages.why_it_matters: Stage 5 and Stage 6 must depend on interfaces, so both can be tested without a database.
entry_criteria: Substage 4.3 (Database schema definition and code generation) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Define repository interfaces in the domain layer, expressed entirely in domain types.
details: No database row type, no generated class and no SQL concept crosses the interface.

work.action: Implement full CRUD for categories, groups, accounts, rule versions, rule lines and settings.
Implement soft delete for every configuration record: set is_deleted and deleted_at_ms, never remove the row.
details: Ensure every read path filters tombstones by default, with an explicit opt-in to include them for sync.

work.action: Implement reactive queries returning streams for everything the dashboard and reports watch.
details: The stream must emit when a row changes through any code path, including a future background sync writer.
Write a test that mutates through a second path and asserts the stream emits.

work.action: Implement list queries with the filters the PRD journeys require: by group, by account, by archived state, by date range.
Implement mapping between database rows and domain entities in one place, with round-trip tests.
details: A round-trip test catches the field that quietly stops being persisted when the schema changes.

work.action: Write repository tests against an in-memory database instance so they are fast and hermetic.

acceptance_criteria: No repository method signature exposes a database or generated type.
Every configuration delete is soft, proven by a test that finds the row still present with a tombstone.
Reactive streams emit on changes made through a different code path, proven by a test.
Row-to-entity mapping round-trips every field, proven per entity.
Repository tests run against an in-memory database with no file system dependency.
must_not: Do not leak persistence types into the domain.
Do not hard-delete a synced record.
common_pitfalls: Read paths that forget to filter tombstones, so deleted categories reappear in pickers.
A mapping function updated for writes but not for reads, losing a field silently.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Append-only ledger and transactional writes
substages.goal: Make INV-03 impossible to violate through the repository API, and make multi-row writes atomic.
substages.why_it_matters: An editable ledger is an unauditable ledger. Enforcing append-only at the API surface is stronger than enforcing it by discipline.
entry_criteria: Substage 4.4 (Repository interfaces and CRUD implementation) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement ledger writes as append-only: an insert method and nothing else.
details: There must be no update method and no delete method on the ledger repository at all.
A correction is a new compensating entry referencing the entry it reverses.

work.action: Implement the income event write as a single atomic transaction covering the event row and every allocation ledger entry.
details: Either all rows commit or none do.
Write a test that injects a failure midway and asserts zero rows remain.

work.action: Implement the spending write and the reversal write with the same atomicity guarantee.
Implement idempotent inserts keyed by the client-generated UUID, so a retry cannot duplicate an entry.
details: This matters in Stage 7, but the guarantee belongs here where the write happens.

work.action: Add a test that attempts, by any available route, to modify an existing ledger row, and demonstrates there is no such route.
details: This is a design test, not a behaviour test; it documents the guarantee for future maintainers.

work.action: Implement the reversal linkage: a reversal entry references its original, and the original is marked as reversed without being altered.
details: State how marked-as-reversed is represented without mutating the immutable row - typically a separate lookup by reverses_entry_id.

acceptance_criteria: The ledger repository exposes no update or delete method.
A failure injected midway through an income event write leaves zero rows, proven by a test.
Inserting the same ledger entry UUID twice is a no-op rather than a duplicate, proven by a test.
Reversal linkage works without altering the original row, proven by a test.
The design test documenting immutability exists and passes.
must_not: Do not add an update path for the ledger for any reason, including data repair - repair is a compensating entry.
Do not represent reversed by mutating the original row.
common_pitfalls: A generic repository base class that supplies update and delete to every table including the ledger.
Non-atomic writes that leave an income event with only some of its allocations, which breaks conservation permanently.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Balance derivation and cache verification
substages.goal: Implement balances as derived values with a recompute-and-compare verifier.
substages.why_it_matters: INV-04. A stored balance that nobody can re-derive is a number nobody can trust after the first sync merge.
entry_criteria: Substage 4.5 (Append-only ledger and transactional writes) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement the derivation query: a category balance is the signed sum of its ledger entries.
details: Verify the query uses the index designed in substage 2.4 by inspecting the query plan.

work.action: Implement period-scoped derivations the engine needs: allocated_in_current_period for fixed-recurring categories.
details: Period boundaries follow the anchor day rule from the design, including the short-month behaviour.
Take the period definition as an input rather than computing it from the system clock here.

work.action: If the design chose a cache table, implement it with explicit invalidation on every ledger write.
details: Never update a cached balance by incrementing it from application code without also being able to recompute it.

work.action: Implement the recompute-and-compare verifier.
details: Recomputes every balance from the ledger and compares against cached or displayed values.
Returns a list of discrepancies rather than throwing, so it can be run as a diagnostic.
Write a test that corrupts a cached balance deliberately and asserts the verifier finds it.

work.action: Implement per-account totals as the sum of the balances of linked categories, and test that they reconcile.
Measure derivation cost against a synthetic ledger at the five-year volume from the PRD, and record the timing.

acceptance_criteria: Every balance is derivable from the ledger alone.
The verifier detects a deliberately corrupted cached balance, proven by a test.
Period-scoped derivation handles an anchor day of 31 through a 28-day February without skipping or duplicating a period.
Per-account totals reconcile with the sum of linked category balances.
Derivation timing at five-year volume is recorded and within the NFR-06 budget.
must_not: Do not expose a setter for a balance.
Do not read the system clock inside a derivation.
common_pitfalls: A cached balance updated on write but never verified, which drifts after a sync merge and is discovered by a user.
Period logic that silently skips February when the anchor day is 30 or 31.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Seed data, suggested categories and the sink
substages.goal: Ship the suggested categories as editable proposals, create the mandatory sink, and make seeding idempotent and non-destructive.
substages.why_it_matters: FR-08 and NFR-04. A first-time budgeter facing an empty app abandons it, and a suggestion the user cannot change is a constraint.
entry_criteria: Substage 4.6 (Balance derivation and cache verification) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement the seed set from the manifest, including each entry's suggested type.
details: Spending, savings and business groups exactly as listed, with the suggested type carried through.

work.action: Flag every seeded record with is_suggested_seed and a seed_version, so a user's own creation is distinguishable from an untouched suggestion.
Seed default percentages that produce a configuration passing every validator.
details: Group split and every within-group split must total exactly 10000 basis points.
Write the test that asserts this before writing the numbers, so a mistake cannot ship.

work.action: Create the sink category per OQ-07: uncapped, non-deletable, renameable, in the agreed group, with is_sink set.
details: If a separate business sink was agreed, create that too.
Assert at seed time that the sink is uncapped, since the engine's termination guarantee depends on it.

work.action: Make seeding idempotent.
details: Running it twice must not duplicate anything.
Prove it with a test comparing row counts and updated_at values before and after a second run.

work.action: Make seeding non-destructive.
details: Editing a seeded category and re-running the seeder must leave the edit intact.
Prove it with a test.

work.action: Externalise every seeded string so localisation is possible later without touching logic.
Implement the reset-to-suggestions path if the design calls for one, and make explicit that it is destructive and confirmed.

acceptance_criteria: Seeding an empty database produces a configuration that passes every validator from substage 4.8.
Default percentages total exactly 10000 at group level and within every group, proven by a test.
Running the seeder twice is a no-op, proven by a test.
A user edit to a seeded category survives a re-run, proven by a test.
The sink exists, is uncapped, and is flagged non-deletable.
Every seeded category can be renamed, retyped, re-ceilinged and removed.
must_not: Do not make any seeded category permanent or uneditable, except the sink's existence.
Do not hardcode seeded strings inside logic.
common_pitfalls: Default percentages that total 9999 because of a hand-computed split, which blocks onboarding.
A seeder that overwrites user edits on every app launch.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Configuration validators and cycle detection
substages.goal: Implement every validation rule from the design and wire it into the write path so invalid state cannot be persisted.
substages.why_it_matters: The engine assumes a valid configuration. This layer is what guarantees it, including after a sync merge.
entry_criteria: Substage 4.7 (Seed data, suggested categories and the sink) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement each validator in the domain layer, returning typed failures rather than throwing.
details: Group basis points total exactly 10000.
Within-group basis points total exactly 10000 for every group with a non-zero share.
A group with a non-zero share has at least one active category.
Ceiling greater than zero when set.
Redirect target exists, is active, and is not the category itself.
FIXED_RECURRING has a bill amount greater than zero and an anchor day within 1 to 31.
The sink exists, is uncapped and is not archived.
An account with linked categories cannot be deleted without reassignment.
Currency and exponent are immutable once any ledger entry exists.

work.action: Implement redirect-graph cycle detection and run it on every save that touches a redirect target.
details: Use a traversal with a visited set over the whole graph, not just the immediate pair.
Test two-node, three-node and longer cycles, plus a self-reference.

work.action: Implement the archive guard: a category that is another category's redirect target cannot be archived, and the error names the dependant.
Wire validators into the repository write path so a caller that forgets to validate still cannot persist invalid state.
details: Validation at the call site alone is not sufficient - Stage 7 will write through a different path.

work.action: Implement the post-merge validation entry point Stage 7 will call, returning a discrepancy list rather than throwing.
Write a test for every rule with both a passing and a failing case.

acceptance_criteria: A two-node redirect cycle is rejected, proven by a test.
A three-node redirect cycle is rejected, proven by a test.
A self-referencing redirect is rejected.
Deleting or archiving the sink is rejected.
Rule lines totalling 9999 and 10001 are both rejected.
Validation cannot be bypassed by writing directly through the repository, proven by a test.
The post-merge validation entry point exists and returns a discrepancy list.
must_not: Do not enforce an invariant-protecting rule only in the UI.
Do not throw from a validator - return a typed failure.
common_pitfalls: Cycle detection that only checks the direct target, missing a three-node loop.
Validation wired into the UI but not the repository, so sync writes bypass it.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Migrations, export and backup
substages.goal: Build the migration framework and its fixture testing, plus a full export and import that round-trips exactly.
substages.why_it_matters: NFR-07. A schema change after release must never cost a user their history, and every user must be able to take their data elsewhere.
entry_criteria: Substage 4.8 (Configuration validators and cycle detection) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement the migration framework with the initial version, even though there is only one version today.
details: The framework existing before it is needed is what makes the first real migration safe.

work.action: Implement the migration test harness: open a fixture database at version N, migrate, assert data intact and schema matching version N plus one.
Commit a fixture database at version 1 now, so the first real migration has something to test against.
details: Populate it with a representative dataset, including a reversal, a redirect and an archived category.

work.action: Implement full JSON export covering every table, including tombstones and sync columns.
details: Amounts as integer minor units, never decimal strings in the machine-readable export.
Include schema version, currency configuration and export timestamp in a header block.

work.action: Implement import that restores an export onto an empty database.
details: Refuse an import whose schema version is newer than the app understands.
Refuse an import whose currency configuration differs from the current install, with a clear explanation.

work.action: Implement the automatic pre-migration export written to app storage before any migration runs.
details: State where it is written and how many are retained.

work.action: Write the round-trip test: export, wipe, import, then assert every balance and every ledger entry is byte-identical.
Measure export duration at the five-year volume and record it.

acceptance_criteria: The migration test harness runs in CI with the version 1 fixture present.
Export, wipe and import reproduces identical balances and ledger contents, proven by a test.
The export header contains schema version and currency configuration.
Import refuses a newer schema version and a mismatched currency, each proven by a test.
A pre-migration export is written automatically, proven by a test.
Export duration at five-year volume is recorded.
must_not: Do not write amounts as floating point in the export.
Do not allow an import that silently drops unknown fields.
common_pitfalls: A migration framework added only when the first migration is needed, under time pressure.
An export that omits tombstones, so importing resurrects deleted records.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Data layer test suite and performance smoke test
substages.goal: Complete the test suite to the coverage target and prove the layer performs at realistic volume.
substages.why_it_matters: Stage 5 must be able to trust this layer completely, and Stage 9 should find nothing here.
entry_criteria: Substage 4.9 (Migrations, export and backup) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Audit coverage per file and list every uncovered line with a justification or a new test.
Ensure every entity has create, read, update where permitted, soft delete, list-with-filters and stream-emission tests.
Ensure the three structural guarantees each have an explicit test: append-only, transactional atomicity and foreign key enforcement.
Ensure seed idempotency, seed non-destructiveness and default configuration validity are each covered.
Ensure every validator has a passing and a failing case.
Test balance derivation against hand-computed expected values, including a category whose history contains a reversal.
details: Hand-computed means computed independently, not copied from the implementation's output.

work.action: Build the synthetic five-year dataset generator from the PRD volume assumptions and commit it as a test utility.
details: Stage 8 and Stage 9 will reuse it, so build it once here and build it well.

work.action: Run the performance smoke test: balance query, date-range query, per-account totals and export, at five-year volume.
details: Record actual timings in the stage report against the NFR-06 targets.

acceptance_criteria: All tests pass and the command output is captured in the stage report.
Domain and data layer coverage is at least 90 percent, with every uncovered line justified.
Balance derivation is verified against independently computed values.
The synthetic dataset generator is committed and reusable.
Performance timings are recorded against their targets.
must_not: Do not copy implementation output into an expected value.
Do not lower the coverage target to pass.
common_pitfalls: Coverage achieved by tests that assert nothing meaningful.
A performance test run on an empty database, which proves nothing.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Data layer documentation and gate preparation
substages.goal: Document the implemented layer, prove it matches the design, and prepare the stage gate.
substages.why_it_matters: Stage 5 depends on a precise statement of what this layer guarantees.
entry_criteria: Substage 4.10 (Data layer test suite and performance smoke test) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Write docs/DATA_LAYER.md.
details: The schema-versus-design comparison table from substage 4.3.
The repository API surface, with the guarantees each method provides.
The seed data policy and how a user's edits are protected.
The migration and backup procedure.
Known limitations.

work.action: State explicitly the guarantees Stage 5 may rely on.
details: Balances are ledger-derived and verifiable.
Ledger entries are immutable and idempotent by UUID.
Configuration reaching the engine has passed validation.
No repository method reads the clock.

work.action: Delete any throwaway inspection harness built during this stage and confirm it is gone.
Update docs/TRACEABILITY.md for the requirements this stage advances.
Write docs/reports/STAGE_4_REPORT.md with test output, coverage figures, performance timings and the comparison table.
Prepare the gate question.

acceptance_criteria: DATA_LAYER.md states the guarantees Stage 5 relies on, explicitly.
The throwaway harness, if any, has been removed and its removal verified.
TRACEABILITY.md is updated.
The stage report contains test output, coverage and timings.
must_not: Do not leave a manual inspection UI in the codebase.
common_pitfalls: Documenting the intended guarantees rather than the implemented ones.

stage_definition_of_done: All data layer tests pass in CI.
Coverage of the domain and data layers is at least 90 percent.
The implemented schema matches SCHEMA.md, evidenced by a comparison table.
Seeding produces a valid, fully editable default configuration.
Export and import round-trip without data loss.
TRACEABILITY.md updated for the requirements this stage advances.
stage_must_not: Do not build UI screens beyond a throwaway harness, and delete that harness before the stage ends.
Do not implement the distribution algorithm here, not even a simplified version.
Do not expose any repository method that updates or deletes a ledger entry.
Do not use hard deletes on synced tables.
Do not store money as a floating point value anywhere, including in export files.
Do not add network or Google account code in this stage.
anti_patterns: A balance column that allocation code increments directly - it drifts and cannot be audited.
Seed data the user cannot edit or remove, which turns suggestions into constraints.
Auto-increment integer primary keys, which collide the first time two offline devices sync.
Repository methods returning database row types, leaking persistence into the domain.

artifacts_next_stage_consumes: Domain entities and the Money type are the engine's inputs and outputs in Stage 5.
Repository interfaces let Stage 5 test the engine with no database at all.
Balance derivation supplies the headroom inputs the engine needs.
Sync columns and tombstones are what Stage 7 merges.
handoff.summary_to_write: State the exact repository interface the engine depends on, and confirm the append-only guarantee is enforced at the API level.

approval_gate.question_to_user: Stage 4 (Data layer) is complete. <N> tests pass, coverage is <X> percent, and the schema matches the approved design. Notable implementation decisions: <list>. Do you approve moving to Stage 5, the distribution engine?
